name: PixiTween Director S8a: browser export and gallery
description: Browser-only export of the Pixi canvas to WebM (and an experimental MP4) with a soundtrack rebuilt from the composition, plus a gallery of finished films and a seed script. No server routes, no deploy (that is S8b).

readFirst: docs/engine/README.md (engine behaviour: composition JSON, Player slot props, layer kinds, effects, validation; read before writing code that touches the engine)
docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md (shared types, file ownership, repo rules)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md (sections 3, 5 and 11: the audio design and the verified engine facts)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/contract-issues.md (which gaps the contract update resolved; what remains)
web/src/player/Player.tsx and web/src/App.tsx (S2) before touching either
extraGuardrails: Export and gallery run in the browser only; no story adds a server route.
Never reach into the engine's audio elements or patch the engine: build the soundtrack from the composition data (design section 3.2).
Use Mediabunny for MP4 (pre-installed by S2, D-9); never install packages in a story; mp4-muxer is deprecated.
Do not edit web/src/App.tsx or web/src/player/Player.tsx: the Export slot and the PlayerHandle are S2 contracts (06 section 2, section 3a, D-7) and ExportPanel.tsx is a stub S8a fills.
manualGates: MG-1 (owner, Chrome): open the M1 film, export WebM, play it in VLC and Chrome. Duration within 0.3 s of the timeline, audio in sync by eye, no frame-0 flash at the end. Repeat with the experimental MP4 in QuickTime if US-010 shipped. Record browser, file size and result in the PR.
MG-1b (owner): with a fixture film on screen, confirm export is not blank (verifies the preserveDrawingBuffer assumption U1 in design section 11).

stories.title: Recorder MIME picker and export file names
stories.description: As an exporter, I want a tested MIME picker and file namer so that every export picks a format the browser supports and gets a clear file name.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.4 (recorder settings, MIME preference order).

Create web/src/export/formats.ts exporting RECORDER_MIME_PREFERENCE (in order: 'video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus', 'video/webm;codecs=vp9', 'video/webm;codecs=vp8,opus', 'video/webm;codecs=vp8', 'video/webm', 'video/mp4').

In the same file export pickRecorderMime(isTypeSupported: (mime: string) => boolean): string | null (first supported entry, else null), extensionForMime(mime: string): 'webm' | 'mp4', and exportFileName(title: string, ext: string, now: Date = new Date()): string.

exportFileName lowercases the title, replaces every run of non-alphanumerics with '-', trims '-' from both ends, cuts the slug to 40 characters, falls back to 'film' when the slug is empty, and appends '-' plus the UTC date as YYYYMMDD, then '.' plus ext.
Create web/src/export/formats.test.ts covering every acceptance case below.
acceptance: pickRecorderMime(() => true) returns 'video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus'
pickRecorderMime(m => m === 'video/webm;codecs=vp8') returns 'video/webm;codecs=vp8', and pickRecorderMime(m => m === 'video/mp4') returns 'video/mp4'
pickRecorderMime(() => false) returns null
exportFileName('Morning Ritual — White Mug!', 'webm', new Date('2026-11-02T12:00:00Z')) returns 'morning-ritual-white-mug-20261102.webm'
exportFileName('', 'mp4', new Date('2026-11-02T12:00:00Z')) returns 'film-20261102.mp4', and a 100-character title yields a slug of at most 40 characters

stories.title: Audio level keyframes to gain points
stories.description: As an exporter, I want audio level keyframes converted to gain points so that the exported soundtrack follows the same volume curve as the player.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.2 and the engine facts E9 and E12 in section 11 (keyframe t is in the containing comp's frames; seconds = (frames - inPointFrames) / fps; a hold keyframe steps at the next keyframe's time).

Create web/src/export/gainCurve.ts exporting type GainPoint = [timeSec: number, value: number] and levelToGainPoints(level: number | undefined | Array<{ t: number; v: number; hold?: boolean }>, fps: number, layerInPointFrames: number): GainPoint[].

Rules: undefined returns [[0, 1]]; a static number returns [[0, max(0, value)]]; keyframes map to ((t - layerInPointFrames) / fps, max(0, v)); a hold keyframe emits [a.time, a.v] then [b.time, a.v] then [b.time, b.v] so the step is explicit; keyframes before 0 s are clipped by interpolating the value at 0 s (linear) and dropping earlier points; when every keyframe is before 0 s return [[0, lastValue]].
Create web/src/export/gainCurve.test.ts with the cases below. Import no engine code; the function takes plain data.
acceptance: levelToGainPoints(undefined, 30, 0) returns [[0, 1]] and levelToGainPoints(-1, 30, 0) returns [[0, 0]]
levelToGainPoints([{t:0,v:0},{t:30,v:0.8}], 30, 15) returns [[0, 0.4], [0.5, 0.8]] (value at 0 s interpolated between -0.5 s and 0.5 s)
levelToGainPoints([{t:0,v:0.2,hold:true},{t:30,v:1}], 30, 0) returns [[0, 0.2], [1, 0.2], [1, 1]]
levelToGainPoints([{t:0,v:0.3},{t:10,v:0.9}], 30, 60) returns [[0, 0.9]] (all keyframes precede the layer start)

stories.title: Collect the export audio plan from a composition
stories.description: As an exporter, I want every audio source in a composition with its absolute start and end so that the export can rebuild the soundtrack without reaching into the engine's audio elements.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 3.2, 4.2 and 5.1, and shared/composition.ts. Note the engine facts: a precomp layer's inner comp is comp.precomps[layer.compId]; inner times are offset by outerOffsetSec + layer.inPoint / outerFps; an inner comp uses its own fps (E8).

Create web/src/export/audioPlan.ts exporting interface AudioPlanItem { layerId: string; assetId: string; src: string; source: 'audio' | 'video'; startSec: number; endSec: number; gain: GainPoint[]; pan?: number } and collectAudioPlan(comp: AepCompositionJson): AudioPlanItem[] (import the type from 'reacthub-pixitweenjs').

Walk comp.layers depth first carrying offsetSec and the asset map (inner assets override outer, as the engine's mergeAssetMaps does). precomp: recurse into comp.precomps?.[layer.compId] with offsetSec + layer.inPoint / currentComp.fps. audio and not hidden: item with startSec = offsetSec + inPoint / fps, endSec = offsetSec + outPoint / fps, gain = levelToGainPoints(layer.level, fps, layer.inPoint), pan = layer.pan when it is a number (first keyframe value when keyframed).

video and muted !== true: item with source 'video', gain [[0, 1]]. Skip layers whose assetId is missing from the asset map or whose asset src is an empty string. Return items sorted by startSec ascending (stable).
Create web/src/export/audioPlan.test.ts using small hand-written compositions typed as AepCompositionJson (cast through unknown where fields are irrelevant).
acceptance: A root audio layer (fps 30, inPoint 30, outPoint 120, asset src '/api/assets/a1', no level) yields startSec 1, endSec 4 and gain [[0, 1]]
A root precomp layer with inPoint 120 whose inner comp (fps 30) holds an audio layer with inPoint 15 and outPoint 75 yields startSec 4.5 and endSec 6.5
Two levels of nesting add both offsets; an inner comp at fps 24 under an outer 30 fps precomp layer with inPoint 60 and an inner audio layer inPoint 24 yields startSec 3
A hidden audio layer, a muted video layer, a layer whose asset is missing and a layer whose asset src is '' are all excluded; an unmuted video layer yields source 'video'
With layers out of order the result is sorted by startSec ascending

stories.title: Mix the audio plan into one AudioBuffer
stories.description: As an exporter, I want the audio plan rendered to a single stereo buffer so that the recorder can add the soundtrack in sync with the canvas.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.3 and web/src/export/audioPlan.ts.

Create web/src/export/mixAudio.ts exporting mixAudio(plan: AudioPlanItem[], durationSec: number, deps?: MixDeps): Promise<{ buffer: AudioBuffer | null; warnings: Array<{ layerId: string; reason: string }> }>. MixDeps has createOfflineContext(channels: number, length: number, sampleRate: number) and loadBuffer(src: string, ctx: BaseAudioContext): Promise<AudioBuffer>; the defaults use the real OfflineAudioContext and fetch + decodeAudioData.

Empty plan: return { buffer: null, warnings: [] } without creating a context. Otherwise create a 2-channel, 44100 Hz context of ceil(durationSec * 44100) frames. For each item: load its buffer (a throw becomes a warning { layerId, reason: message } and the item is skipped), create a buffer source with start(item.startSec) and stop(item.endSec), a gain node following item.gain (setValueAtTime for the first point and for each duplicate time, linearRampToValueAtTime otherwise, times offset by item.startSec), and a stereo panner when item.pan is a number. Connect source, gain, optional panner, then the context destination.
When every item failed to load return buffer null with the warnings; otherwise await startRendering() and return its buffer.
Create web/src/export/mixAudio.test.ts with a FakeOfflineContext class that records createBufferSource, createGain, createStereoPanner, start, stop and gain automation calls; jsdom has no Web Audio.
acceptance: Two items (startSec 1 / endSec 4 and startSec 4.5 / endSec 6.5) produce two sources whose start() and stop() receive exactly those times
An item with gain [[0, 0], [1, 0.8]] and startSec 4.5 records setValueAtTime(0, 4.5) and linearRampToValueAtTime(0.8, 5.5)
When loadBuffer throws for one of two items the other is still mixed and warnings contains { layerId: <the failing layer>, reason: <the message> }
An empty plan returns { buffer: null, warnings: [] } and createOfflineContext is never called; when all items fail buffer is null
The context is created with 2 channels, sampleRate 44100 and length ceil(durationSec * 44100)

stories.title: Export types, canvas access and drawing-buffer check
stories.description: As an exporter, I want typed errors and a small player adapter so that recording code never depends on the Player's internals.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 3a "Player" (PlayerHandle = { getCanvas, getApp, play, pause, seek(sec), getTime }, created with preserveDrawingBuffer default true, time in seconds) and web/src/player/Player.tsx (S2) for where the PlayerHandle type is exported.

Create web/src/export/types.ts exporting type ExportErrorCode = 'no-canvas' | 'unsupported' | 'tab-hidden' | 'aborted' | 'recorder-error' | 'timeout', class ExportError extends Error { code: ExportErrorCode }, interface ExportDriver { play(): void; pause(): void; seek(sec: number): void; getTime(): number }, and type ExportPlayerHandle = Pick<PlayerHandle, 'getCanvas' | 'play' | 'pause' | 'seek' | 'getTime'> (import the PlayerHandle type from the Player module).

Create web/src/export/playerCanvas.ts exporting getExportCanvas(handle: ExportPlayerHandle | null): HTMLCanvasElement (throws ExportError('no-canvas') when the handle or its canvas is null), isDrawingBufferPreserved(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement): boolean | null (asks canvas.getContext('webgl2') then canvas.getContext('webgl'); returns getContextAttributes()?.preserveDrawingBuffer === true, or null when neither context is available), and playerToDriver(handle: ExportPlayerHandle): ExportDriver.
Create web/src/export/playerCanvas.test.ts using plain fake objects for the canvas and handle.
acceptance: getExportCanvas(null) throws an ExportError whose code is 'no-canvas', and so does a handle whose getCanvas() returns null
isDrawingBufferPreserved returns true for a fake canvas whose context reports preserveDrawingBuffer true, false when it reports false, and null when getContext returns null for both context types
playerToDriver returns an object whose play, pause, seek and getTime delegate to the handle (verified with vi.fn)
new ExportError('no-canvas', 'x') has name 'ExportError' and code 'no-canvas'

stories.title: recordCanvas: capture the canvas and audio with MediaRecorder
stories.description: As an exporter, I want a recorder that plays the film once and returns a WebM blob so that users can download their film without any render server.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 3.1, 4.3 and 5.4, plus the engine facts E2, E3 and E5 (the timeline seeks to 0 before GSAP_COMPLETE, so stop on time, not on the event; totalDuration includes a 0.2 s buffer).

Create web/src/export/recordCanvas.ts exporting recordCanvas(opts: RecordOptions, deps?: RecordDeps): Promise<Blob> with RecordOptions as in design 4.3 (canvas, driver, durationSec, fps default 30, audio, mimeType, videoBitsPerSecond default 8_000_000, onProgress, signal). RecordDeps injects MediaRecorderCtor, AudioContextCtor, MediaStreamCtor, raf, now for tests.

Sequence: driver.seek(0); await two animation frames; stream = new MediaStream(canvas.captureStream(fps).getVideoTracks()); when audio is present create an AudioContext, a MediaStreamDestination and a buffer source for the AudioBuffer, connect the source to the destination only (never to ctx.destination) and add the destination's audio tracks to the stream; create new MediaRecorder(stream, { mimeType, videoBitsPerSecond, audioBitsPerSecond: 128000 only when audio is present }); collect ondataavailable chunks; recorder.start(250).

In recorder.onstart: start the audio source then driver.play(). A requestAnimationFrame loop reads driver.getTime(), calls onProgress({ timeSec, fraction: min(1, time / durationSec) }), and when time >= durationSec - 1 / fps it calls driver.pause(), stops the audio source, recorder.stop(); on recorder.onstop resolve new Blob(chunks, { type: mimeType }).

signal abort: pause the driver, stop the audio source and recorder, stop all tracks, reject with ExportError('aborted'). Create web/src/export/recordCanvas.test.ts with fake MediaRecorder (static isTypeSupported, fires onstart synchronously after start, onstop after stop), a fake canvas whose captureStream returns an object with getVideoTracks, a fake AudioContext, and a scripted driver.
acceptance: The recorded event order for a film with audio is ['seek:0', 'recorder.start', 'audio.start', 'play']
With durationSec 2, fps 30 and scripted driver times 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 1.94 the recorder stops once, after the 1.94 reading (1.94 >= 2 - 1/30), and the driver is paused
The returned Blob has type equal to the mimeType option and a size equal to the sum of the fake chunks
onProgress fractions never decrease and the last one is at least 0.97

Without audio the stream holds only the video track and MediaRecorder is built with { mimeType, videoBitsPerSecond: 8000000 } and no audioBitsPerSecond; with audio it is built with audioBitsPerSecond 128000
Aborting through the AbortSignal rejects with an ExportError whose code is 'aborted' and calls driver.pause once and recorder.stop once

stories.title: recordCanvas guards: hidden tab, timeout, recorder error
stories.description: As an exporter, I want the recorder to fail fast and clean up when the tab is hidden, the timeline stalls or the recorder errors so that users never get a silent bad file.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 5.5 and 7 and web/src/export/recordCanvas.ts.

Edit web/src/export/recordCanvas.ts: register a document 'visibilitychange' listener while recording; when document.visibilityState becomes 'hidden' abort with ExportError('tab-hidden'). Remove the listener in every exit path.
Add a hard timeout of durationSec + 5 seconds measured with deps.now(); if the driver never reaches the stop time, pause the driver, stop the recorder and reject with ExportError('timeout').

Handle recorder.onerror: stop all tracks, pause the driver, reject with ExportError('recorder-error') whose message includes the browser's error text. Make every rejection path idempotent (cleanup runs once).
Extend web/src/export/recordCanvas.test.ts with fake timers or an injected clock for these three cases.
acceptance: Dispatching visibilitychange with document.visibilityState 'hidden' mid-recording rejects with code 'tab-hidden' and removes the listener (removeEventListener called with the same function)
A driver stuck at time 0 with an injected clock advanced past durationSec + 5 rejects with code 'timeout' and pauses the driver
A fake recorder that fires onerror with message 'boom' rejects with code 'recorder-error' and a message containing 'boom'
In every rejection case driver.pause and recorder.stop are called at most once and all tracks are stopped

stories.title: ExportPanel: export button, progress, cancel, download
stories.description: As a viewer, I want an Export button with progress and a download link so that I can save my film as a video file from the browser.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 3.1 and 7, web/src/export/*.ts (all helpers), the S2 stub web/src/panels/ExportPanel.tsx and how web/src/App.tsx renders the Export slot (06-contracts.md section 2 and D-7: S8a fills the stub; App.tsx is not edited), and an existing panel such as web/src/panels/NewFilm.tsx for styling and test conventions.

Fill web/src/panels/ExportPanel.tsx. Keep the props the stub and App.tsx already define (the film and a way to reach the Player handle); if the stub has no props, derive the film from the same source App uses for the Player. Add an optional second prop deps?: { recordCanvas?: typeof recordCanvas; mixAudio?: typeof mixAudio; now?: () => Date } for tests. From the film use composition, title and the PlayerHandle.

States: idle shows a button labelled 'Export video'; it is disabled with the text "Your browser can't record video. Try Chrome." when MediaRecorder or canvas.captureStream is missing, and disabled with 'Nothing to export' when composition is null or has zero duration. Running shows an element with role 'progressbar' (aria-valuenow 0-100) and a 'Cancel' button. Done shows an anchor with download = exportFileName(filmTitle ?? 'film', ext, now()) and href from URL.createObjectURL, plus a 'Dismiss' button that revokes the URL.

Flow on click: durationSec = composition.durationInFrames / composition.fps; plan = collectAudioPlan(composition); mix = await mixAudio(plan, durationSec); mimeType = pickRecorderMime(MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported); recordCanvas with the canvas from getExportCanvas(getPlayer()) and playerToDriver. Show 'Exported without audio' when the plan was non-empty but mix.buffer is null, and 'Exported without audio from: <layer ids>' for warnings. Show "Export may produce blank frames in this browser." when isDrawingBufferPreserved(canvas) === false.
Create web/src/panels/ExportPanel.test.tsx with React Testing Library and injected deps (fake recordCanvas resolving a Blob, scripted onProgress).
acceptance: With MediaRecorder undefined the button is disabled and the text "Your browser can't record video. Try Chrome." is visible
Clicking Export calls the injected recordCanvas once with durationSec equal to durationInFrames / fps and the canvas returned by the PlayerHandle's getCanvas()
After the fake recorder reports progress 0.5 the progressbar has aria-valuenow 50, and clicking Cancel aborts the AbortSignal passed to recordCanvas
When recordCanvas resolves, an anchor with download 'morning-ritual-20261102.webm' appears for filmTitle 'Morning Ritual' and a fixed clock of 2026-11-02, and Dismiss calls URL.revokeObjectURL
When the plan has one item and mixAudio returns buffer null the text 'Exported without audio' is shown; when isDrawingBufferPreserved is false the blank-frames warning is shown

stories.title: Optional MP4 export with Mediabunny
stories.description: As a viewer, I want an experimental MP4 download so that I can open the film in QuickTime, which may not play WebM.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.6 and 06-contracts.md D-9: mp4-muxer is deprecated and S2 pre-installs mediabunny. Verify that package.json lists mediabunny and that node_modules/mediabunny exists; if it is missing set notes to 'blocked: mediabunny missing (S2 D-9)' and stop; do not install it here.

Create web/src/export/mp4Export.ts exporting mp4Supported(deps?: { VideoEncoder?: typeof VideoEncoder }): Promise<boolean> (false when VideoEncoder is undefined; otherwise await VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported({ codec: 'avc1.640028', width: 1280, height: 720 }) and return its supported flag) and exportMp4(opts: { canvas: HTMLCanvasElement; driver: ExportDriver; durationSec: number; fps?: number; audio?: AudioBuffer | null; onProgress?: RecordOptions['onProgress']; signal?: AbortSignal }, deps?: { mediabunny?: typeof import('mediabunny'); raf?: typeof requestAnimationFrame }): Promise<Blob>.

exportMp4 builds new Output({ format: new Mp4OutputFormat(), target: new BufferTarget() }), a CanvasSource(canvas, { codec: 'avc', quality: new Quality('high') }) added with output.addVideoTrack, and an AudioBufferSource({ codec: 'aac', quality: new Quality('high') }) with output.addAudioTrack only when audio is present. await output.start(); seek(0); play; in the animation-frame loop await videoSource.add(timeSec, 1 / fps) with the driver's time; at durationSec - 1 / fps pause, await audioSource.add(audio) when present, await output.finalize(), return new Blob([output.target.buffer], { type: 'video/mp4' }).

Edit web/src/panels/ExportPanel.tsx: when await mp4Supported() is true show a second option 'MP4 (experimental)'; selecting it calls exportMp4 instead of recordCanvas; the file name extension becomes mp4.
Create web/src/export/mp4Export.test.ts with vi.mock('mediabunny') capturing constructor arguments and call order, and extend web/src/panels/ExportPanel.test.tsx for the format option.
acceptance: mp4Supported returns false when VideoEncoder is undefined and true when isConfigSupported resolves { supported: true }
exportMp4 constructs Output with an Mp4OutputFormat and a BufferTarget, CanvasSource with codec 'avc', and AudioBufferSource with codec 'aac' only when audio is passed
The recorded call order is output.start, then videoSource.add with increasing timestamps, then audioSource.add, then output.finalize
The returned Blob has type 'video/mp4' and the size of the fake target buffer
The panel shows the 'MP4 (experimental)' option only when mp4Supported resolves true, and choosing it makes the download name end in '.mp4'

stories.title: Gallery model: ready films to gallery items
stories.description: As a visitor, I want finished films listed with a thumbnail, duration and badge so that I can pick one to replay.
steps: Read 06-contracts.md section 3 (FilmState, AssetRef, Storyboard) at docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md, docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 4.1, and shared/composition.ts. Import FilmState with whichever alias S2 configured (see tsconfig.json paths).

Create web/src/panels/gallery/model.ts exporting interface GalleryItem { id; title; aspect; durationSec; thumbUrl; sceneCount; hasGenerated } as in design 4.1, toGalleryItems(films: FilmState[]): GalleryItem[] (newest first), and formatDuration(sec: number): string.

toGalleryItems keeps only films with status 'ready' and a composition, sorted newest first by FilmState.createdAt (ISO string, 06 section 3; compare with Date.parse; a missing or invalid createdAt sorts last; ties keep the input order). durationSec = round(composition.durationInFrames / composition.fps, one decimal). title falls back to 'Untitled film'. thumbUrl = the url of the asset whose id equals brief.productAssetId, else '/api/assets/' + brief.productAssetId. sceneCount = storyboard?.scenes.length ?? 0; hasGenerated = storyboard?.scenes.some(s => s.mode === 'generate') ?? false.
formatDuration returns m:ss with the seconds rounded to the nearest whole second.

Create web/src/panels/gallery/model.test.ts with three FilmState fixtures built inline: a ready film with a 'generate' scene (durationInFrames 360, fps 30, 3 scenes, createdAt '2026-11-01T10:00:00Z'), a ready motion-only film (createdAt '2026-11-02T09:00:00Z'), and a film with status 'building'.
acceptance: From the three fixtures toGalleryItems returns two items, newest first (the motion-only film, then the generate film); the 'building' film is excluded

The generate film's item has durationSec 12, sceneCount 3, hasGenerated true and thumbUrl equal to the url of the asset matching brief.productAssetId; the motion-only item has hasGenerated false; a ready film with no createdAt sorts after both
A film whose assets array lacks the product asset gets thumbUrl '/api/assets/<productAssetId>' and a film with no title gets title 'Untitled film'
formatDuration(12) returns '0:12', formatDuration(75) returns '1:15' and formatDuration(59.6) returns '1:00'

stories.title: Seed film fixture for the gallery
stories.description: As an owner, I want a small valid demo film as data so that a fresh deploy has something in its gallery.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 3 (FilmState, FilmVersion), fixtures/seed/README.md (mug-product.png) and the real fixture shapes in docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 4.

Create fixtures/s08a/seed-films/demo-mug/seed.json with { film: <FilmState-like object with status 'ready', title 'Morning Ritual - White Ceramic Mug', aspect '16:9', a storyboard of 3 scenes (ids scene-1-hero-reveal, scene-2-pour with mode 'generate', scene-3-detail; 4 s each) and a composition>, assets: [{ key: 'mug-product', file: '../../../seed/mug-product.png', mime: 'image/png', role: 'product-photo' }] }.

The composition is hand-written: version '1.0.0', id 'demo-mug', width 1920, height 1080, fps 30, durationInFrames 360, bgColor '#2b1d14', one shape layer {kind:'shape', id:'bg', inPoint:0, outPoint:360, transform:{position:[960,540], anchor:[960,540], scale:[1,1], rotation:0, opacity:1}, path:{kind:'rect', size:[1920,1080]}, fill:'#2b1d14'} and one image layer {kind:'image', id:'mug', assetId:'mug', inPoint:0, outPoint:360, transform:{position:[960,540], anchor:[192,336], scale:[1.2,1.2], rotation:0, opacity:1}} with assets {mug:{type:'image', src:'{{asset:mug-product}}', width:384, height:672}}.
The asset reference in film.brief.productAssetId and in composition.assets src uses the placeholder token {{asset:mug-product}}, which the seed script replaces with the real URL.

Create fixtures/s08a/seed-films/demo-mug/seed.test.ts: substitute the placeholder with '/api/assets/x' and check the composition with parseAepCompositionSafe imported from 'reacthub-pixitweenjs' (add '// @vitest-environment jsdom' at the top if importing the package root fails in Node).
acceptance: parseAepCompositionSafe on the substituted composition reports success
The seed film has status 'ready', 3 storyboard scenes and exactly one scene with mode 'generate'
The referenced file fixtures/seed/mug-product.png exists relative to seed.json
A composition with the placeholder left in place still parses (the placeholder is only a string src)

stories.title: Seed script: copy demo films into the data stores
stories.description: As an owner, I want npx tsx scripts/seed-gallery.ts to load the demo films so that a fresh deploy shows a gallery.
steps: Read server/store/film-store.ts, server/store/asset-store.ts and server/test-utils/film.ts (S2) for the FilmStore and AssetStore APIs and how to construct them against a directory, and fixtures/s08a/seed-films/demo-mug/seed.json.

Create scripts/seed-gallery.ts exporting prepareSeed(seed, urlFor: (key: string) => string) (pure: replaces every {{asset:<key>}} token in the film and composition with urlFor(key) and returns the film init and composition) and runSeed(opts: { films: FilmStore; assets: AssetStore; seedDir: string; force?: boolean; log?: (m: string) => void }): Promise<{ created: number; skipped: number }>.

runSeed: for each directory under seedDir read seed.json; skip (count skipped, log 'already seeded: <title>') when films.list() already has a film with the same title unless force; otherwise put each asset file with assets.put(bytes, mime, { role }), call prepareSeed with assets.url(ref.id), films.create(init) with brief.productAssetId set to the new asset id, films.commit(id, composition, 'director', 'seed') and films.update(id, { status: 'ready', storyboard, title }).

Add a main guard so that running the file directly constructs the stores on the data directory from the validated env object in server/env.ts (DATA_DIR, default ./data; read env.ts for the accessor), reads --force from argv and prints the counts. Never import or run it at module load time in tests.
Create scripts/seed-gallery.test.ts using makeTestFilm() from server/test-utils/film.ts for temp stores.
acceptance: On empty temp stores runSeed returns { created: 1, skipped: 0 } and films.list() then holds one film with status 'ready' whose composition validates
A second runSeed returns { created: 0, skipped: 1 }; with force: true it returns { created: 1, skipped: 0 }
The created film's brief.productAssetId refers to an asset that assets.read() can load and whose bytes equal fixtures/seed/mug-product.png
prepareSeed leaves no '{{asset:' substring in its output
